claims.text: DFT-informed machine-learning algorithms can improve determination of solid-to-fluid transition temperature in multicomponent high-entropy materials.
DFT-informed machine-learning algorithms can improve determination of fusion enthalpy and entropy, volume change, and dense-fluid heat capacity.
Machine-learning algorithms can efficiently screen the large compositional space of high-entropy alloys.
High-throughput DFT-based modeling can screen hundreds of thousands of multicomponent high-entropy-alloy candidates.
Configurational entropy is a key driver that a model can use to predict the stated transition properties.
Mixing enthalpy is an important thermodynamic driver in high-entropy-alloy formation and stability.
Binary enthalpic interactions can reproduce the mixing enthalpy of higher-component random solid solutions.
Configurational entropy and mixing enthalpy provide a causal basis for predicting solid-to-fluid transition temperature and fusion properties.
The proposed approach applies in high-temperature states, potentially above 800 K.
The proposed approach will be more accurate than existing experiments, TOR-TILD, and conventional DFT free-energy studies.
Existing experimental methods, TOR-TILD, and DFT free-energy studies constitute the comparison baseline.
Applicability is limited to systems for which DFT calculations are feasible and adequate machine-learning training data are available.
Generalization of the machine-learning models across all high-entropy-alloy classes is uncertain.
The accuracy of DFT for complex multicomponent systems is uncertain.
The hypothesis would be falsified if prediction errors exceed a predefined threshold for a majority of experimentally tested alloys.
